description: An eight-stage shift register clocked at a quarter of the incoming rate, with a three-stage register clocked at a third of it, and an XOR input for making pseudo-random patterns by self-patching

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V advances an internal counter; the main register shifts on every fourth edge and the triplet register on every third
A rising edge clears both registers and the counter
The bit shifted into both registers, read as a one whenever it is above 1V
Exclusive-ORed with the data bit as it enters both registers, read as a one whenever it is above 1V; patching a later stage output back here makes a linear feedback shift register

outputs.text: Carries 10V while that stage of the main eight-stage register holds a one, and 0V otherwise
The eleven stages as one polyphonic cable, the first eight channels carrying the main register and the last three the triplet register
Carries 10V while that stage of the three-stage triplet register holds a one, and 0V otherwise

notes: feed it a clock at four times the rate the main outputs should move at, since the register shifts once every four clock pulses
nothing moves and nothing comes out until a clock is patched; the data input on its own changes nothing
the counter runs to twelve and wraps, so the main and triplet registers line up again every twelve clock pulses
the Beta expander goes immediately to the right of this module and turns the register into pitch voltages
